claim: Intermediate filaments (IFs) are major components of the metazoan cytoskeleton.
source: Intermediate filaments (IFs) are major components of the metazoan cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about intermediate filaments.

claim: There is a long-standing debate about whether IF network organization only reflects or also determines cell and tissue function.
source: A long-standing debate concerns the question whether IF network organization only reflects or also determines cell and tissue function.
evidence: This statement references an ongoing scientific debate in the field.

claim: Mutants of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) SMA-5 perturb the organization of the intestinal IF cytoskeleton resulting in luminal widening and cytoplasmic invaginations.
source: Using Caenorhabditis elegans, we have recently described mutants of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) SMA-5 which perturb the organization of the intestinal IF cytoskeleton resulting in luminal widening and cytoplasmic invaginations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Besides structural phenotypes, systemic dysfunctions were observed in sma-5 mutants.
source: Besides these structural phenotypes, systemic dysfunctions were also observed.
evidence: This statement refers to previously described observations.

claim: The IF polypeptide IFB-2 is a highly efficient suppressor of both the structural and functional deficiencies of mutant sma-5 animals.
source: We now identify the IF polypeptide IFB-2 as a highly efficient suppressor of both the structural and functional deficiencies of mutant sma-5 animals by removing the aberrant IF network.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: IFB-2 suppresses sma-5 phenotypes by removing the aberrant IF network.
source: We now identify the IF polypeptide IFB-2 as a highly efficient suppressor of both the structural and functional deficiencies of mutant sma-5 animals by removing the aberrant IF network.
evidence: This mechanistic explanation is supported by experimental observations in the study.

claim: Perturbed IF network morphogenesis is linked to hyperphosphorylation of multiple sites throughout the entire IFB-2 molecule.
source: Mechanistically, perturbed IF network morphogenesis is linked to hyperphosphorylation of multiple sites throughout the entire IFB-2 molecule.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The rescuing capability of IFB-2 is IF isotype-specific.
source: The rescuing capability is IF isotype-specific and not restricted to sma-5 mutants but extends to mutants that disrupt the function of the cytoskeletal linker IFO-1 and the IF-associated protein BBLN-1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing different IF polypeptides.

claim: The rescuing capability of IFB-2 is not restricted to sma-5 mutants but extends to mutants that disrupt the function of IFO-1 and BBLN-1.
source: The rescuing capability is IF isotype-specific and not restricted to sma-5 mutants but extends to mutants that disrupt the function of the cytoskeletal linker IFO-1 and the IF-associated protein BBLN-1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on double mutants presented in the manuscript.

claim: The findings provide strong evidence for adverse consequences of deranged IF networks.
source: The findings provide strong evidence for adverse consequences of the deranged IF networks with implications for diseases that are characterized by altered IF network organization.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results presented in the study.

claim: IFs mediate mechanical tissue stability.
source: They mediate mechanical tissue stability and have been implicated in multiple cellular processes such as vesicle transport, organelle positioning, cell cycle regulation, differentiation, metabolism, motility, and stress response (Etienne-Manneville, 2018; Jacob et al., 2018; Leube and Schwarz, 2016; Margiotta and Bucci, 2016; Yoon and Leube, 2019; Coch et al., 2020; Toivola et al., 2010; Geisler and Leube, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: IFs have been implicated in vesicle transport, organelle positioning, cell cycle regulation, differentiation, metabolism, motility, and stress response.
source: They mediate mechanical tissue stability and have been implicated in multiple cellular processes such as vesicle transport, organelle positioning, cell cycle regulation, differentiation, metabolism, motility, and stress response (Etienne-Manneville, 2018; Jacob et al., 2018; Leube and Schwarz, 2016; Margiotta and Bucci, 2016; Yoon and Leube, 2019; Coch et al., 2020; Toivola et al., 2010; Geisler and Leube, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: There is an ongoing debate about whether IFs are simply bystanders of cellular processes or contribute actively to cell function and dysfunction.
source: An ongoing debate is whether IFs are simply bystanders of these cellular processes or contribute actively to cell function and dysfunction (Etienne-Manneville, 2018; Bott and Winckler, 2020; Ridge et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement references an ongoing scientific debate supported by citations.

claim: Six IF polypeptides (IFB-2, IFC-1, IFC-2, IFD-1, IFD-2, and IFP-1) co-localize in the apical cytoplasm of the C. elegans intestine.
source: A striking example of specialized IF network organization is encountered in the intestine, where six IF polypeptides IFB-2, IFC-1, IFC-2, IFD-1, IFD-2, and IFP-1 co-localize in the apical cytoplasm and form the electron dense endotube, which surrounds the lumen as a compact fibrous sheath and is attached to the composite C. elegans apical junction (CeAJ) (Carberry et al., 2009; Jahnel et al., 2016; Bossinger et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The six IF polypeptides form the electron dense endotube, which surrounds the lumen as a compact fibrous sheath.
source: A striking example of specialized IF network organization is encountered in the intestine, where six IF polypeptides IFB-2, IFC-1, IFC-2, IFD-1, IFD-2, and IFP-1 co-localize in the apical cytoplasm and form the electron dense endotube, which surrounds the lumen as a compact fibrous sheath and is attached to the composite C. elegans apical junction (CeAJ) (Carberry et al., 2009; Jahnel et al., 2016; Bossinger et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The endotube is attached to the composite C. elegans apical junction (CeAJ).
source: A striking example of specialized IF network organization is encountered in the intestine, where six IF polypeptides IFB-2, IFC-1, IFC-2, IFD-1, IFD-2, and IFP-1 co-localize in the apical cytoplasm and form the electron dense endotube, which surrounds the lumen as a compact fibrous sheath and is attached to the composite C. elegans apical junction (CeAJ) (Carberry et al., 2009; Jahnel et al., 2016; Bossinger et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The localization of the intestinal IF network is evolutionarily conserved.
source: It is assumed that this evolutionary conserved localization of the intestinal IF network (Coch and Leube, 2016) provides protection against mechanical stress (Geisler and Leube, 2016; Toivola et al., 2010; Geisler et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The intestinal IF network provides protection against mechanical stress.
source: It is assumed that this evolutionary conserved localization of the intestinal IF network (Coch and Leube, 2016) provides protection against mechanical stress (Geisler and Leube, 2016; Toivola et al., 2010; Geisler et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The endotube is positioned at the interface between the cortical actin cytoskeleton with the stiff microvillar brush border and the soft cytoplasm.
source: Accordingly, the endotube is positioned at the interface between the cortical actin cytoskeleton with the stiff microvillar brush border and the soft cytoplasm (Geisler et al., 2020; McGhee, 2007; Bossinger et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The IF-rich endotube likely dampens mechanical stresses occurring during food intake, defecation, and body movement.
source: Because of its high degree of elasticity the IF-rich endotube likely dampens mechanical stresses occurring during food intake, defecation, and body movement (Geisler et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by a citation.

claim: Elimination of IFB-2, IFC-2, and IFD-2 leads to luminal widening.
source: Elimination of the intestinal IFs IFB-2, IFC-2, and IFD-2 therefore leads to luminal widening although loss of IFC-1, IFD-1, and IFP-1 does not (Geisler et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Loss of IFC-1, IFD-1, and IFP-1 does not lead to luminal widening.
source: Elimination of the intestinal IFs IFB-2, IFC-2, and IFD-2 therefore leads to luminal widening although loss of IFC-1, IFD-1, and IFP-1 does not (Geisler et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: IFC-2 mutants have a rarefied endotube.
source: Electron microscopy revealed that IFC-2 mutants have a rarefied endotube, whereas IFB-2 mutants lack it completely (Geisler et al., 2019; Geisler et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: IFB-2 mutants lack the endotube completely.
source: Electron microscopy revealed that IFC-2 mutants have a rarefied endotube, whereas IFB-2 mutants lack it completely (Geisler et al., 2019; Geisler et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Intestinal IF mutants present very mild organismal phenotypes with only minor or no detectable effects on development, progeny production, survival, and stress sensitivity with the exception of IFC-2 mutants.
source: The intestinal IF mutants present very mild organismal phenotypes with only minor or no detectable effects on development, progeny production, survival, and stress sensitivity with the exception of IFC-2 mutants, which cause additional excretory canal defects (Geisler et al., 2020; Al-Hashimi et al., 2018; Carberry et al., 2009; Karabinos et al., 2001; Karabinos et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: IFC-2 mutants cause additional excretory canal defects.
source: The intestinal IF mutants present very mild organismal phenotypes with only minor or no detectable effects on development, progeny production, survival, and stress sensitivity with the exception of IFC-2 mutants, which cause additional excretory canal defects (Geisler et al., 2020; Al-Hashimi et al., 2018; Carberry et al., 2009; Karabinos et al., 2001; Karabinos et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: SMA-5 is a stress-activated kinase orthologue of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) type.
source: One of them is SMA-5, a stress-activated kinase orthologue of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) type (Watanabe et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The C. elegans WormBase lists MAPK7 (BMK1; ERK4; ERK5; PRKM7) as the closest orthologue of SMA-5 in vertebrates.
source: The C. elegans WormBase (version WS287; https://wormbase.org) lists MAPK7 (BMK1; ERK4; ERK5; PRKM7) as its closest orthologue in vertebrates.
evidence: This statement is based on database information.

claim: MAPK7 activity has not been linked to IFs so far.
source: However, MAPK7 activity has not been linked to IFs so far.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of evidence in the literature.

claim: Abundant cytoplasmic invaginations of the adluminal, apical plasma membrane develop over time in loss-of-function sma-5(n678) mutant intestines.
source: Abundant cytoplasmic invaginations of the adluminal, apical plasma membrane develop over time in loss-of-function sma-5(n678) mutant intestines (Geisler et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The structural changes in sma-5(n678) mutants correlate with the development of a locally thickened endotube consisting of amorphous material next to areas with complete endotube loss.
source: These changes correlate with the development of a locally thickened endotube consisting of amorphous material next to areas with complete endotube loss.
evidence: This is an observation from previous work referenced in the introduction.

claim: The cytoplasmic invaginations in sma-5(n678) mutants form at the transition between areas with thickened endotube and areas with complete endotube loss.
source: The cytoplasmic invaginations form at the transition between both areas.
evidence: This is an observation from previous work referenced in the introduction.

claim: The structural changes in sma-5(n678) mutants go along with altered IFB-2 phosphorylation.
source: The structural changes go along with biochemical changes, that is, altered IFB-2 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is an observation from previous work referenced in the introduction.

claim: In comparison to the wild type and to intestinal IF mutants, sma-5 mutants are smaller, produce less offspring, develop more slowly, live shorter, and are more sensitive to microbial pathogens and osmotic as well as oxidative stress.
source: Furthermore, in comparison to the wild type and to intestinal IF mutants sma-5 mutants are smaller, produce less offspring, develop more slowly, live shorter, and are more sensitive to microbial pathogens and osmotic as well as oxidative stress (Geisler et al., 2016; Geisler et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: It is not known whether the pathologies in sma-5(n678) mutants are attributable to the altered IF cytoskeleton or other sma-5(n678)-dependent cellular perturbations.
source: It is not known whether these pathologies are attributable to the altered IF cytoskeleton or other sma-5(n678)-dependent cellular perturbations.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: IFO-1 was originally identified as a cellular defense gene against pore-forming toxins and as part of the MAPK/JNK innate immune defense network.
source: Another modulator of the intestinal IF cytoskeleton is the intestinal IF organizer gene ifo-1 (Carberry et al., 2012), which was originally identified as a cellular defense gene against pore-forming toxins and as part of the MAPK/JNK innate immune defense network (referred to as ttm-4 in Kao et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The IF network in loss-of-function ifo-1 mutants collapses into large aggregates, which accumulate primarily at the CeAJ and occasionally in the cytoplasm.
source: The IF network in loss-of-function ifo-1 mutants collapses into large aggregates, which accumulate primarily at the CeAJ and occasionally in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is an observation from previous work referenced in the introduction.

claim: ifo-1 mutants are small, have reduced progeny, and are hypersensitive to different types of stress.
source: ifo-1 mutants are small, have reduced progeny, and are hypersensitive to different types of stress.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The phenotypes of ifo-1 mutants are not only much more pronounced than those observed in IF mutants but are also more pronounced than in sma-5 mutants.
source: The phenotypes are not only much more pronounced than those observed in IF mutants but are also more pronounced than in sma-5 mutants (Geisler et al., 2019; Geisler et al., 2020; Carberry et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The contribution of the deranged IF network to the ifo-1 mutant phenotype has not been determined to date.
source: Again, the contribution of the deranged IF network to the ifo-1 mutant phenotype has not been determined to date.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap.

claim: BBLN-1 is a small coiled-coil protein whose depletion results in an intestinal phenotype that is highly reminiscent of that observed in sma-5 mutants presenting bubble-shaped cytoplasmic invaginations of the apical plasma membrane.
source: Recently, we described a third type of intestinal IF regulator, namely BBLN-1 (Remmelzwaal et al., 2021). BBLN-1 is a small coiled-coil protein whose depletion results in an intestinal phenotype that is highly reminiscent of that observed in sma-5 mutants presenting bubble-shaped cytoplasmic invaginations of the apical plasma membrane.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Systemic consequences of bbln-1 mutation have not been analyzed in detail to date.
source: Systemic consequences of bbln-1 mutation have not been analyzed in detail to date.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap.

claim: SMA-5, IFO-1, and BBLN-1 have been localized to the apical submembrane compartment in intestinal cells.
source: Remarkably, all three regulators have been localized to the apical submembrane compartment in intestinal cells (Remmelzwaal et al., 2021; Geisler et al., 2016; Carberry et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A suppressor screen of sma-5(n678) mutants identified ifb-2 mutation as the most efficient suppressor.
source: To identify components of the IF regulatory pathways in the C. elegans intestine, we performed a suppressor screen of sma-5(n678) mutants, which identified ifb-2 mutation as the most efficient suppressor.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study.

claim: Loss-of-function ifb-2 mutation partially rescued the ifo-1 and bbln-1 phenotypes.
source: Loss-of-function ifb-2 mutation also partially rescued the ifo-1 and bbln-1 phenotypes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study.

claim: The perturbed intestinal IF networks were completely depleted in all instances of ifb-2 mutation rescue.
source: The perturbed intestinal IF networks were completely depleted in all instances.
evidence: This is an observation from the current study.

claim: The systemic dysfunctions in sma-5, ifo-1, and bbln-1 mutants were also rescued for the most part by ifb-2 mutation.
source: Even more importantly, the systemic dysfunctions were also rescued for the most part.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study.

claim: The findings provide new evidence on the gain-of-toxic-function hypothesis driving the pathogenesis of aggregate-forming diseases.
source: These findings provide new evidence on the gain-of-toxic-function hypothesis driving the pathogenesis of aggregate-forming diseases, which have been shown to involve aberrant IF networks (e.g., Coulombe et al., 2009; Chamcheu et al., 2011; Yoshida and Nakagawa, 2012; Clemen et al., 2013; Gentil et al., 2015; Didonna and Opal, 2019).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings with citations to relevant disease contexts.

claim: Two lines were isolated from the suppressor screen in which native IFB-2 expression could not be detected by immunoblotting.
source: Selecting for fast developing lines we isolated two lines, in which we were not able to detect any native IFB-2 expression by immunoblotting (data not shown).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: An 83 bp deletion was identified in the ifb-2 gene locus (positions 5.751.812–5.751.893; allele ifb-2(kc20)).
source: We therefore focused on the ifb-2 gene locus for further analysis and identified an 83 bp deletion (positions 5.751.812–5.751.893; allele ifb-2(kc20)).
evidence: This is a molecular characterization from the current study.

claim: Due to the frameshift, the mutant ifb-2(kc20) gene encodes only 120 amino acids, consisting of the entire 31 amino acid-long head domain, 85 amino acids of the coiled-coil rod domains 1a and 1b, and the four additional carboxyterminal amino acids R-G-P-S.
source: Due to the resulting frameshift the mutant ifb-2 gene encodes only 120 amino acids, consisting of the entire 31 amino acid-long head domain, 85 amino acids of the coiled-coil rod domains 1a and 1b (Karabinos et al., 2004), and the four additional carboxyterminal amino acids R-G-P-S.
evidence: This is a molecular characterization from the current study with a citation for domain information.

claim: sma-5(n678) mutants were crossed with the ifb-2 knockout allele kc14 to demonstrate that loss-of-function of IFB-2 is sufficient and necessary to rescue the sma-5(n678) phenotype.
source: To demonstrate that loss-of-function of IFB-2 is by itself sufficient and necessary to rescue the sma-5(n678) phenotype and to exclude that the residual aminoterminal part of IFB-2 that is still produced from kc20 is responsible for the rescue, we crossed sma-5(n678) mutants with the previously described ifb-2 knockout allele kc14 (Geisler et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes an experimental approach with a citation to the kc14 allele.

claim: The kc14 allele encodes a 29 amino acid-long oligopeptide encompassing only 13 of the most aminoterminal amino acids of IFB-2.
source: The kc14 allele encodes a 29 amino acid-long oligopeptide encompassing only 13 of the most aminoterminal amino acids of IFB-2.
evidence: This is a molecular characterization.

claim: Assessment of body length revealed a near normal body size of the double sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
source: Assessment of body length revealed a near normal body size of the double sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: Only a minor reduction in body length was detected at day 4 after egg laying in sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) mutants as was the case for ifb-2(kc14) single mutants.
source: Only a minor reduction was detected at day 4 after egg laying as was the case for ifb-2(kc14) single mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Normal body length was reached by day 5 in sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) and ifb-2(kc14) but not in sma-5(n678).
source: Normal body length was reached by day 5 in sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) and ifb-2(kc14) but not in sma-5(n678) (not shown).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: Light microscopy revealed a rescue of the luminal widening and cytoplasmic invagination phenotypes in sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants.
source: Light microscopy revealed a rescue of the luminal widening and cytoplasmic invagination phenotypes (Figure 1A–D′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Dextran feeding experiments confirmed the rescue of luminal widening and cytoplasmic invagination phenotypes.
source: Dextran feeding experiments confirmed these observations (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Ultrastructural analyses showed a reversion of the phenotype to a near wild-type situation in the double mutants.
source: Ultrastructural analyses further showed a reversion of the phenotype to a near wild-type situation in the double mutants (Figure 1E–H′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Only minor luminal undulations and slight perturbation of the microvillar brush border remained in sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants.
source: Only minor luminal undulations and slight perturbation of the microvillar brush border remained.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: The endotube was completely absent in sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants.
source: Most notably, the endotube was completely absent (Figure 1H–H′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The ultrastructural features of sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants were identical to those encountered in ifb-2(kc14) single mutants.
source: The ultrastructural features were identical to those encountered in ifb-2(kc14) single mutants (Figure 1G–G′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The ifb-2(kc14) knockout allele restored the prolonged time of development of sma-5(n678).
source: The ifb-2(kc14) knockout allele furthermore restored the prolonged time of development of sma-5(n678) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The developmental time of sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants was still elevated in comparison to the wild type but only slightly different from the single ifb-2(kc14) mutant.
source: While still elevated in comparison to the wild type, developmental time was only slightly different from the single ifb-2(kc14) mutant.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: The single ifb-2(kc14) and double sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) mutants showed high degree of similarity in the developmental time course.
source: The results shown in Figure 2B illustrate the high degree of similarity in the developmental time course of the single ifb-2(kc14) and double sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Both ifb-2(kc14) and sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) developed more slowly than the wild type and much faster than the sma-5(n678) animals.
source: Both developed more slowly than the wild type and much faster than the sma-5(n678) animals, 7.1% of which never reached adulthood.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: 7.1% of sma-5(n678) animals never reached adulthood.
source: Both developed more slowly than the wild type and much faster than the sma-5(n678) animals, 7.1% of which never reached adulthood.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: The larval arrest in sma-5(n678) could be ascribed to arrest at the L4 stage.
source: The latter could be ascribed to larval arrest at the L4 stage (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The shortened median life span of sma-5(n678) animals could be rescued in the sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants to the level observed in ifb-2(kc14) single mutants.
source: Life span determinations further showed that the shortened median life span of sma-5(n678) animals could be rescued in the sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants to the level observed in ifb-2(kc14) single mutants.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: The life spans of sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) and ifb-2(kc14) mutants were still reduced in comparison to the wild type by 1 day.
source: Yet, the life spans of sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) and ifb-2(kc14) mutants were still reduced in comparison to the wild type by 1 day (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The drastic reduction in progeny of sma-5(n678) was rescued in the double mutant to the level observed in ifb-2(kc14).
source: Similarly, the drastic reduction in progeny of sma-5(n678) was rescued in the double mutant to the level observed in ifb-2(kc14), which, again, was significantly less than in the wild type (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The progeny of ifb-2(kc14) was significantly less than in the wild type.
source: Similarly, the drastic reduction in progeny of sma-5(n678) was rescued in the double mutant to the level observed in ifb-2(kc14), which, again, was significantly less than in the wild type (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: In the presence of oxidative stress, the survival of sma-5(n678) was reduced by 3.5 hr in comparison to wild-type N2.
source: In the presence of oxidative stress, the survival of sma-5(n678) was reduced by 3.5 hr in comparison to wild-type N2 but was only reduced by 0.5 hr and 1.5 hr in ifb-2(kc14) and sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14), respectively (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: In the presence of oxidative stress, the survival of ifb-2(kc14) was reduced by 0.5 hr in comparison to wild-type N2.
source: In the presence of oxidative stress, the survival of sma-5(n678) was reduced by 3.5 hr in comparison to wild-type N2 but was only reduced by 0.5 hr and 1.5 hr in ifb-2(kc14) and sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14), respectively (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: In the presence of oxidative stress, the survival of sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14) was reduced by 1.5 hr in comparison to wild-type N2.
source: In the presence of oxidative stress, the survival of sma-5(n678) was reduced by 3.5 hr in comparison to wild-type N2 but was only reduced by 0.5 hr and 1.5 hr in ifb-2(kc14) and sma-5(n678);ifb-2(kc14), respectively (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: All mutants appeared to be similarly affected in osmotic stress assays and a statistically significant rescue phenotype could not be observed.
source: All mutants appeared to be similarly affected in osmotic stress assays and a statistically significant rescue phenotype could not be observed (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Loss of IFB-2 rescues all major sma-5(n678) phenotypes, except osmotic stress hypersensitivity, to levels observed in ifb-2(kc14).
source: Taken together, we can conclude that loss of IFB-2 rescues all major sma-5(n678) phenotypes, except osmotic stress hypersensitivity, to levels observed in ifb-2(kc14).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Intestinal IF network perturbations adversely affect organismal physiology.
source: This demonstrates that intestinal IF network perturbations adversely affect organismal physiology.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Each IF was downregulated by RNAi in the sma-5(n678) background to test whether the observed rescue is specific for IFB-2.
source: To test whether the observed rescue is specific for IFB-2 or applies also to the other five IFs that are expressed in the intestine, each IF was downregulated by RNAi in the sma-5(n678) background.
evidence: This describes an experimental approach.

claim: ifb-2(RNAi) efficiently rescued the developmental growth defect in sma-5(n678).
source: The assays confirmed the expected efficient rescue of the developmental growth defect in sma-5(n678) by ifb-2(RNAi).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: An easily detectable, though reduced rescuing efficiency was detected for ifc-2(RNAi).
source: An easily detectable, though reduced rescuing efficiency was detected for ifc-2(RNAi).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: An even less pronounced but statistically still significant rescue could be identified in ifd-1, ifd-2, and ifp-1 RNAi-treated animals.
source: An even less pronounced but statistically still significant rescue could be identified in ifd-1, ifd-2, and ifp-1 RNAi-treated animals and none for ifc-1(RNAi).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: No rescue was observed for ifc-1(RNAi).
source: An even less pronounced but statistically still significant rescue could be identified in ifd-1, ifd-2, and ifp-1 RNAi-treated animals and none for ifc-1(RNAi).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: ifb-2(RNAi) abolished the reporter fluorescence as well as the cytoplasmic invaginations of sma-5(n678).
source: As predicted, ifb-2(RNAi) abolished the reporter fluorescence as well as the cytoplasmic invaginations of sma-5(n678).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: ifc-2(RNAi) led to a reduction of the cytoplasmic invagination phenotype but was much less efficient than ifb-2(RNAi).
source: ifc-2(RNAi) also led to a reduction of the cytoplasmic invagination phenotype but was much less efficient than ifb-2(RNAi).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: All other interfering RNAs (besides ifb-2 and ifc-2) did not visibly affect the invagination phenotype.
source: All other interfering RNAs, however, did not visibly affect the invagination phenotype.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: IFB-2 was essential for IFC-2, IFD-1, and IFD-2 network formation.
source: While IFB-2 was essential for IFC-2, IFD-1, and IFD-2 network formation, IFC-1 and IFP-1 were still able to form a network-like structure at the subapical domain, although only to a very limited extent.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: IFC-1 and IFP-1 were still able to form a network-like structure at the subapical domain after ifb-2(RNAi), although only to a very limited extent.
source: While IFB-2 was essential for IFC-2, IFD-1, and IFD-2 network formation, IFC-1 and IFP-1 were still able to form a network-like structure at the subapical domain, although only to a very limited extent.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: IFC-1 and IFP-1 fluorescence was not due to expression of the respective endogenous genes but due to fosmids, which may have resulted in overexpression.
source: Note, however, that IFC-1 and IFP-1 fluorescence was not due to expression of the respective endogenous genes but due to fosmids, which may have resulted in overexpression.
evidence: This is a methodological note about the experimental system.

claim: The isotype-specific phenotypes can be explained by the heteropolymerization of the different IF polypeptides and their abundance.
source: Taken together, the isotype-specific phenotypes can be explained by the heteropolymerization of the different IF polypeptides and their abundance.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: IFB-2 has been shown to pair with multiple intestinal IFs.
source: Thus, IFB-2 has been shown to pair with multiple intestinal IFs (Karabinos et al., 2017) and has been identified as the main regulator of the endotube (Geisler et al., 2020 and results of this study).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work and current results.

claim: IFB-2 has been identified as the main regulator of the endotube.
source: Thus, IFB-2 has been shown to pair with multiple intestinal IFs (Karabinos et al., 2017) and has been identified as the main regulator of the endotube (Geisler et al., 2020 and results of this study).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work and current results.

claim: IFB-2 depletion elicits the strongest rescuing activity of the sma-5(n678) mutant phenotype.
source: It is therefore not surprising that IFB-2 depletion elicits the strongest rescuing activity of the sma-5(n678) mutant phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: IFC-2 depletion provides the second strongest rescuing activity.
source: It is also in line with IFC-2 depletion providing the second strongest rescuing activity, as also evidenced in previously reported effects on endotube structure and stress sensitivity (Geisler et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The altered IF network rather than loss of a single IF is responsible for the observed rescue of the sma-5(n678) phenotype.
source: Overall, our findings demonstrate that the altered IF network rather than loss of a single IF is responsible for the observed rescue of the sma-5(n678) phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: The head domains of mammalian IF polypeptides have been implicated in cytoplasmic IF assembly.
source: In search for a molecular mechanism that may be involved in altered IF network morphogenesis, it is of interest that the head domains of mammalian IF polypeptides have been implicated in cytoplasmic IF assembly (Omary et al., 2006; Zhou et al., 2021; Hatzfeld and Burba, 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Base pairs 4–1107 of the ifb-2 gene were deleted by CRISPR-cas resulting in a truncated protein missing the complete aminoterminal head domain (ifb-2(mib169[S2-M43 deleted])II).
source: We deleted base pairs 4–1107 of the ifb-2 gene by CRISPR-cas resulting in a truncated protein missing the complete aminoterminal head domain (ifb-2(mib169[S2-M43 deleted])II) (cf. Karabinos et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a molecular characterization from the current study.

claim: ifb-2(mib169) mutants showed a phenotype reminiscent of that described for sma-5(n678) animals with cytoplasmic invaginations of the intestinal lumen accompanied by a rarefied IFC-2 fluorescence.
source: Mutants showed a phenotype reminiscent of that described for sma-5(n678) animals with cytoplasmic invaginations of the intestinal lumen accompanied by a rarefied IFC-2 fluorescence with regions completely lacking a signal next to areas showing enhanced fluorescence (Figure 4A–B').
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The observations on ifb-2 head deletion provide evidence for the evolutionary conserved importance of the IF head domain for IF network formation.
source: These observations provide evidence for the evolutionary conserved importance of the IF head domain for IF network formation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Phosphorylation sites in the head domain of IFs are most frequently targeted by kinases with major consequences on IF network dynamics and organization.
source: Previous observations had also shown that phosphorylation sites in the head domain of IFs are most frequently targeted by kinases with major consequences on IF network dynamics and organization (review in Sawant and Leube, 2017; Snider and Omary, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Wormbase and Phosida list multiple serine phosphorylation sites in the IFB-2 head domain.
source: In accordance, Wormbase and Phosida list multiple serine phosphorylation sites in the IFB-2 head domain.
evidence: This statement is based on database information.

claim: Phosphomimetic S>D and phosphorylation-deficient S>A mutations were introduced into all serines of the IFB-2 head region (S2, S5, S7, S16-S19, S24, and S35) resulting in alleles kc22 and kc26.
source: We therefore decided to mutate putative phosphorylation targets in the IFB-2 head domain by introducing phosphomimetic S>D and phosphorylation-deficient S>A mutations into all serines of the head region, namely S2, S5, S7, S16-S19, S24, and S35 (alleles kc22 and kc26, respectively).
evidence: This describes an experimental approach.

claim: Neither the phosphomimetic nor the phosphorylation-deficient mutant animals presented a visible change in IFC-2 localization.
source: Neither the phosphomimetic nor the phosphorylation-deficient mutant animals presented a visible change in IFC-2 localization (Figure 4C–E′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The ifb-2 head S>D and S>A mutants showed no developmental delay.
source: Further characterization revealed that the mutants showed no developmental delay (Figure 4G) and only a slight reduction of progeny in case of the ifb-2 head S>D mutants (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Only a slight reduction of progeny was observed in the ifb-2 head S>D mutants.
source: Further characterization revealed that the mutants showed no developmental delay (Figure 4G) and only a slight reduction of progeny in case of the ifb-2 head S>D mutants (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Significant reduction of life span could be observed in all ifb-2 head domain mutant instances.
source: However, significant reduction of life span could be observed in all instances (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The phosphorylation sites in the head domain of IFB-2 are not necessary for IF network morphogenesis per se.
source: Taken together, while the phosphorylation sites in the head domain of IFB-2 are not necessary for IF network morphogenesis per se, they may affect network properties such as subunit turnover that are not readily apparent from static pictures and may result in reduced network resilience leading to the decreased life span.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The phosphorylation sites in the head domain of IFB-2 may affect network properties such as subunit turnover that are not readily apparent from static pictures.
source: Taken together, while the phosphorylation sites in the head domain of IFB-2 are not necessary for IF network morphogenesis per se, they may affect network properties such as subunit turnover that are not readily apparent from static pictures and may result in reduced network resilience leading to the decreased life span.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Allele ifb-2(kc27) codes for an IFB-2 mutant containing S2/S5/S7/S16−19>A mutations and a deletion of the region E31-A184.
source: During the course of CRISPR mutagenesis, we isolated allele ifb-2(kc27). This allele codes for an IFB-2 mutant containing not only the intended S2/S5/S7/S16−19>A mutations but a deletion of the region E31-A184, corresponding to the coil 1A, linker L1 and a large part of the coil 1B domain (see Figure 5).
evidence: This is a molecular characterization from the current study.

claim: The deletion in ifb-2(kc27) corresponds to the coil 1A, linker L1 and a large part of the coil 1B domain.
source: This allele codes for an IFB-2 mutant containing not only the intended S2/S5/S7/S16−19>A mutations but a deletion of the region E31-A184, corresponding to the coil 1A, linker L1 and a large part of the coil 1B domain (see Figure 5).
evidence: This is a molecular characterization from the current study.

claim: ifb-2(kc27) mutant animals showed an aberrant IFC-2 fluorescence pattern presenting a reduced though still apically localized IFC-2 distribution with additional, strongly fluorescent granules next to the CeAJ.
source: Interestingly, ifb-2(kc27) mutant animals showed an aberrant IFC-2 fluorescence pattern presenting a reduced though still apically localized IFC-2 distribution with additional, strongly fluorescent granules next to the CeAJ (Figure 4F–F′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The mutant protein in ifb-2(kc27) could be detected by immunofluorescence in the intestine, albeit at highly reduced levels in the cytoplasm, at the CeAJ and in CeAJ-associated granules.
source: The mutant protein could be detected by immunofluorescence in the intestine, albeit at highly reduced levels in the cytoplasm, at the CeAJ and in CeAJ-associated granules (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The truncated IFB-2a and IFB-2c proteins in ifb-2(kc27) are about 50 kDa.
source: The truncated IFB-2a and IFB-2c proteins of about 50 kDa were identified in immunoblots (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Significant effects on progeny and life expectancy were noted in ifb-2(kc27) mutants.
source: Significant effects on progeny and life expectancy were also noted (Figure 4H–I).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The aminoterminal region of IFB-2 up to A184 has an important function in network formation.
source: We therefore propose that the aminoterminal region of IFB-2 up to A184 has an important function in network formation but that mutants lacking this region still retain the ability to enrich apically at the CeAJ.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Mutants lacking the aminoterminal region of IFB-2 up to A184 still retain the ability to enrich apically at the CeAJ.
source: We therefore propose that the aminoterminal region of IFB-2 up to A184 has an important function in network formation but that mutants lacking this region still retain the ability to enrich apically at the CeAJ.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Altered phosphorylation status of the phosphorylation sites in the head domain are not solely responsible for the phenotype observed in SMA-5.
source: Together, we conclude that altered phosphorylation status of the phosphorylation sites in the head domain are not solely responsible for the phenotype observed in SMA-5.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: Mass spectrometry was performed on protein fractions obtained from synchronized wild-type N2 and sma-5(n678) adult animals.
source: To find out whether phosphorylation sites other than those in the head domain may be regulated in sma-5 mutants, we performed mass spectrometry on protein fractions obtained from synchronized wild-type N2 and sma-5(n678) adult animals (Figure 5, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes an experimental approach.

claim: Eight different serine and tyrosine phosphorylation sites spread over the entire rod and tail domains of IFB-2 were identified.
source: We identified eight different serine and tyrosine phosphorylation sites spread over the entire rod and tail domains.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: Phosphopeptides containing S308, S422, Y253, Y335, and Y491 were only found in sma-5(n678).
source: Remarkably, phosphopeptides containing S308, S422, Y253, Y335, and Y491 were only found in sma-5(n678).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: Phosphorylated S92 was detected in all four mutant samples and only in one of four wild-type samples.
source: Furthermore, phosphorylated S92 was detected in all four mutant samples and only in one of four wild-type samples.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: An equal frequency of phosphopeptide detection was observed in mutant and wild-type samples for S55 and S383 (4/4 and 2/4 samples, respectively).
source: An equal frequency of phosphopeptide detection was observed in mutant and wild-type samples for S55 and S383 (4/4 and 2/4 samples, respectively).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: Loss of SMA-5 is accompanied by hyperphosphorylation of IFB-2 affecting multiple phosphorylation sites.
source: In summary, we can conclude that loss of SMA-5 is accompanied by hyperphosphorylation of IFB-2 affecting multiple phosphorylation sites.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mass spectrometry data.

claim: It will be very difficult or even impossible to unequivocally link hyperphosphorylation of defined sites in intestinal IFs to compromised sma-5 activity given the large combinatorial realm of phosphorylation sites.
source: Given the large combinatorial realm of these phosphorylation sites and the likelihood that co-polymerizing intestinal IF polypeptides are also hyperphosphorylated, it will be very difficult or even impossible to unequivocally link hyperphosphorylation of defined sites in intestinal IFs to compromised sma-5 activity.
evidence: This is a discussion of the limitations of the approach.

claim: The observations prove that SMA-5 is involved in regulating IFB-2 phosphorylation.
source: Nevertheless, our observations prove that SMA-5 is involved in regulating IFB-2 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: IFB-2 is unlikely a direct target of SMA-5.
source: They also indicate that IFB-2 is unlikely a direct target of SMA-5.
evidence: This is an inference based on the hyperphosphorylation observation.

claim: SMA-5 may act on IFB-2 phosphorylation by regulating the activity or recruitment of a phosphatase or by an even more indirect mechanism.
source: Further experiments are needed to unravel how SMA-5 acts on IFB-2 phosphorylation, which may be accomplished by regulating the activity or recruitment of a phosphatase or by an even more indirect mechanism.
evidence: This is a speculative discussion of possible mechanisms.

claim: ifo-1(kc2) was crossed with ifb-2(kc14) to test the hypothesis that perturbed IF network organization per se exerts adverse effects.
source: The above findings suggested that the rescue function of IFB-2 deletion in sma-5(n678) was caused by removal of the densely packed IFs. To test the hypothesis that perturbed IF network organization per se exerts adverse effects, we studied another paradigm, namely the ifo-1(kc2) phenotype, which is characterized by prominent IF polypeptide-containing junctional aggregates (Carberry et al., 2012). To this end, we crossed ifo-1(kc2) with ifb-2(kc14).
evidence: This describes an experimental approach with a citation.

claim: The ifo-1(kc2) phenotype is characterized by prominent IF polypeptide-containing junctional aggregates.
source: To test the hypothesis that perturbed IF network organization per se exerts adverse effects, we studied another paradigm, namely the ifo-1(kc2) phenotype, which is characterized by prominent IF polypeptide-containing junctional aggregates (Carberry et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The ifo-1(kc2);ifb-2(kc14) double mutant lacked the junctional IF aggregates altogether.
source: As predicted, the double mutant lacked the junctional IF aggregates altogether (Figure 6A–D′′).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Occasionally, a faint but largely reduced remnant endotube structure was detectable in ifo-1(kc2);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants, often in the vicinity of the CeAJ.
source: Occasionally, a faint but largely reduced remnant endotube structure was detectable, often in the vicinity of the CeAJ.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: ifo-1(kc2);ifb-2(kc14) double mutants had an almost normal intestinal lumen and microvilli.
source: Furthermore, double mutants had an almost normal intestinal lumen and microvilli (Figure 6D–D′′, Figure 1—figure supplement 2 for quantification of luminal dilation).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The time of development of ifo-1(kc2);ifb-2(kc14) was significantly reduced in comparison to ifo-1(kc2).
source: Additional analyses showed a significantly reduced time of development of ifo-1(kc2);ifb-2(kc14) in comparison to ifo-1(kc2), which was, however, still significantly retarded in comparison to ifb-2(kc14) or wild-type N2 (Figure 7A–E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The time of development of ifo-1(kc2);ifb-2(kc14) was still significantly retarded in comparison to ifb-2(kc14) or wild-type N2.
source: Additional analyses showed a significantly reduced time of development of ifo-1(kc2);ifb-2(kc14) in comparison to ifo-1(kc2), which was, however, still significantly retarded in comparison to ifb-2(kc14) or wild-type N2 (Figure 7A–E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Analysis of body length revealed a significant rescue of the ifo-1(kc2) growth defect in the absence of the IFB-2 protein.
source: Moreover, analysis of body length revealed a significant rescue of the ifo-1(kc2) growth defect in the absence of the IFB-2 protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Depletion of IFB-2 rescues the intestinal cytoplasmic invagination phenotype of bbln-1 mutants.
source: It had been shown recently that depletion of IFB-2 rescues the intestinal cytoplasmic invagination phenotype of bbln-1 mutants (Remmelzwaal et al., 2021, Figure 1—figure supplement 2 for quantification of luminal dilation).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and figure reference.

claim: bbln-1(mib70) loss-of-function mutants exhibited systemic dysfunctions as determined by body size and time of development.
source: We found that the bbln-1(mib70) loss-of-function mutants exhibited systemic dysfunctions as determined by body size and time of development (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 8A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The systemic dysfunctions in bbln-1(mib70) were less pronounced than in sma-5(n578) or ifo-1(kc2).
source: Although BBLN-1 expression is, in contrast to IFO-1 and SMA-5, not limited to the intestine, the systemic dysfunctions were less pronounced than in sma-5(n578) or ifo-1(kc2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: The ifb-2(kc14) knockout allele rescued the reduced body size and prolonged time of development of bbln-1(mib70).
source: The ifb-2(kc14) knockout allele rescued the reduced body size and prolonged time of development of bbln-1(mib70) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 8A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: The remaining growth defect and developmental retardation in bbln-1(mib70);ifb-2(kc14) were still slightly increased not only in comparison to the wild type but also to single ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
source: The remaining growth defect and developmental retardation, however, were still slightly increased not only in comparison to the wild type but also to single ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: The single ifb-2(kc14) and double bbln-1(mib70);ifb-2(kc14) mutants showed high degree of similarity in the developmental time course.
source: The results shown in Figure 8B–E highlight the high degree of similarity in the developmental time course of the single ifb-2(kc14) and double bbln-1(mib70);ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by figure data.

claim: Both ifb-2(kc14) and bbln-1(mib70);ifb-2(kc14) develop more slowly than the wild type and much faster than bbln-1(mib70) animals.
source: Both develop more slowly than the wild type and much faster than bbln-1(mib70) animals.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: The complex phenotypes induced by mutation of the MAPK orthologue SMA-5 can be rescued by deletion of the cytoskeletal IF protein IFB-2.
source: Exploiting rapid C. elegans genetic screening, we observed that the complex phenotypes induced by mutation of the MAPK orthologue SMA-5 can be rescued by deletion of the cytoskeletal IF protein IFB-2.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings.

claim: The rescue by IFB-2 deletion included rescue of structural defects (cytoplasmic invagination and lumen dilatation), developmental and growth defects, as well as oxidative stress resilience.
source: This included rescue of structural defects (cytoplasmic invagination and lumen dilatation), developmental and growth defects, as well as oxidative stress resilience.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The obtained rescue levels coincided precisely with the mild phenotype of single ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
source: The obtained rescue levels coincided precisely with the mild phenotype of single ifb-2(kc14) mutants.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Osmotic stress resilience could not be rescued by IFB-2 deletion.
source: Remarkably, osmotic stress resilience could not be rescued suggesting that this loss-of-function is tightly coupled to the absence of the endotube.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the current study.

claim: Osmotic stress resilience loss-of-function is tightly coupled to the absence of the endotube.
source: Remarkably, osmotic stress resilience could not be rescued suggesting that this loss-of-function is tightly coupled to the absence of the endotube.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: It has been suggested that osmotic stress resilience is a fundamental function of cytoplasmic IFs.
source: In accordance, it has been suggested that osmotic stress resilience is a fundamental function of cytoplasmic IFs (D'Alessandro et al., 2002, Pekny and Lane, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Osmotic challenges are of particular relevance to the intestine and its exposure to microbial toxins.
source: Osmotic challenges are of particular relevance to the intestine and its exposure to microbial toxins.
evidence: This is a statement of biological knowledge.

claim: The findings provide strong in vivo evidence that the sma-5 mutant phenotype is caused by the presence of IFB-2-containing pathological assemblies.
source: Our findings furthermore provide strong in vivo evidence that the sma-5 mutant phenotype is caused by the presence of IFB-2-containing pathological assemblies.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Removal of the pathological IFB-2 assemblies also rescued complex biological functions in ifo-1 and bbln-1 mutants.
source: This conclusion was confirmed in ifo-1 and bbln-1 mutants. Removal of the pathological IFB-2 assemblies also rescued complex biological functions.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The deranged intestinal IF cytoskeletons are associated with a gain-of-toxic function exerting negative effects.
source: We therefore conclude that the deranged intestinal IF cytoskeletons are associated with a gain-of-toxic function exerting negative effects, which have detrimental consequences for cell and tissue function and thereby adversely affect growth and reproduction of the entire organism.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: The deranged intestinal IF cytoskeletons have detrimental consequences for cell and tissue function and thereby adversely affect growth and reproduction of the entire organism.
source: We therefore conclude that the deranged intestinal IF cytoskeletons are associated with a gain-of-toxic function exerting negative effects, which have detrimental consequences for cell and tissue function and thereby adversely affect growth and reproduction of the entire organism.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: The scenario is reminiscent of that described in vertebrate disease paradigms, in which IF depletion has positive effects on disease outcome.
source: The scenario is reminiscent of that described in vertebrate disease paradigms, in which IF depletion has positive effects on disease outcome (review in Ridge et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: The fact that removal of the very differently deranged IF networks rescued the phenotypes in all instances is quite remarkable.
source: The fact that removal of the very differently deranged IF networks, that is the thick subapical slabs in sma-5(n678) and bbln-1(mib70) and the large junctional aggregates in ifo-1(kc2), rescued the phenotypes in all instances is quite remarkable since the mechanical and structural dysfunctions appear to be fundamentally different in the different mutant backgrounds.
evidence: This is a discussion of the significance of the findings.

claim: The mechanical and structural dysfunctions appear to be fundamentally different in the different mutant backgrounds (sma-5, bbln-1, and ifo-1).
source: The fact that removal of the very differently deranged IF networks, that is the thick subapical slabs in sma-5(n678) and bbln-1(mib70) and the large junctional aggregates in ifo-1(kc2), rescued the phenotypes in all instances is quite remarkable since the mechanical and structural dysfunctions appear to be fundamentally different in the different mutant backgrounds.
evidence: This is an observation about the different phenotypes.

claim: The dysfunctions manifest in sma-5 and bbln-1 mutants as prominent cytoplasmic invaginations and primarily as luminal widening in ifo-1 mutants.
source: They manifest in sma-5 and bbln-1 mutants as prominent cytoplasmic invaginations and primarily as luminal widening in ifo-1 mutants (see also Geisler et al., 2016; Carberry et al., 2012; Remmelzwaal et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The absence of an endotube in ifo-1 mutants predicts that the force equilibrium is affected differently from that in sma-5 and bbln-1 mutants with the locally thickened endotube.
source: Furthermore, the absence of an endotube in ifo-1 mutants predicts that the force equilibrium is affected differently from that in sma-5 and bbln-1 mutants with the locally thickened endotube.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations.

claim: Restored mechanics alone are not sufficient to explain the phenotypic restoration in the double mutants.
source: This indicates that restored mechanics alone are not sufficient to explain the phenotypic restoration in the double mutants.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Other non-mechanical functions must be attributable to the abnormal IF assemblies.
source: Thus, other non-mechanical functions must be attributable to the abnormal IF assemblies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: IFs may serve as signaling platforms by providing a large scaffold capable of sequestering and positioning signaling molecules.
source: It is interesting in this context that IFs may serve as signaling platforms by providing a large scaffold capable of sequestering and positioning signaling molecules that can be recruited by weak interactions and can be released, for example, by protein modification or structural changes of the IF cytoskeleton (review in Bott and Winckler, 2020; Coulombe and Omary, 2002; Magin et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to reviews.

claim: Future experiments will be needed to show whether such a scaffolding function is compromised in sma-5, bbln-1, and ifo-1 mutants.
source: Future experiments will be needed to show whether such a scaffolding function is compromised in sma-5, bbln-1, and ifo-1 mutants by either sequestering or setting free regulatory factors that modulate pathways needed for normal growth, development, and stress responses.
evidence: This is a discussion of future research directions.

claim: IFs are hyperphosphorylated in sma-5(n678) animals and not hypophosphorylated as would be expected in case of a direct SMA-5/IF interaction.
source: By focusing on IF phosphorylation, we could show that IFs are hyperphosphorylated in sma-5(n678) animals and not hypophosphorylated as would be expected in case of a direct SMA-5/IF interaction.
evidence: This is a summary of the phosphorylation findings.

claim: SMA-5 regulates IF phosphorylation indirectly.
source: This implies that SMA-5 regulates IF phosphorylation indirectly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the hyperphosphorylation observation.

claim: It remains to be shown whether SMA-5 regulates IF phosphorylation by controlling the activity or the recruitment of a phosphatase.
source: It remains to be shown whether this is mediated by controlling the activity or the recruitment of a phosphatase.
evidence: This is a discussion of possible mechanisms.

claim: Activation of an unidentified phosphatase would restore normal IF phosphorylation levels and IF network morphogenesis in sma-5(n678) mutants.
source: This scenario predicts that activation of this yet unidentified phosphatase would restore normal IF phosphorylation levels and IF network morphogenesis in sma-5(n678) mutants.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the proposed mechanism.

claim: An alternative explanation would invoke an even more indirect mechanism whereby SMA-5 phosphorylates a factor that affects IF assembly, which in turn modulates IFB-2 phosphorylation.
source: An alternative explanation would invoke an even more indirect mechanism whereby SMA-5 phosphorylates a factor that affects IF assembly, which in turn modulates IFB-2 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a discussion of alternative mechanisms.

claim: It is not known whether IF phosphorylation is also altered in bbln-1(mib70) and ifo-1(kc2).
source: We do not know whether IF phosphorylation is also altered in bbln-1(mib70) and ifo-1(kc2) and whether IF hyperphosphorylation is per se able to induce IF network aggregation.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap.

claim: It is not known whether IF hyperphosphorylation is per se able to induce IF network aggregation.
source: We do not know whether IF phosphorylation is also altered in bbln-1(mib70) and ifo-1(kc2) and whether IF hyperphosphorylation is per se able to induce IF network aggregation.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap.

claim: The notion of phosphorylation-dependent IF network morphogenesis is in line with numerous publications that have implicated phosphorylation in the regulation of IF assembly and disassembly.
source: The notion of phosphorylation-dependent IF network morphogenesis, however, is in line with numerous publications that have implicated phosphorylation in the regulation of IF assembly and disassembly (reviews in Sawant and Leube, 2017; Nishimura et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to reviews.

claim: IF phosphoepitopes are increased in IF aggregates.
source: It is furthermore supported by the observation that IF phosphoepitopes are increased in IF aggregates (Sawant and Leube, 2017; Sawant et al., 2018; Wöll et al., 2007; Battaglia et al., 2019; Binukumar et al., 2013).
